en: Of or relating to punishment.
Subject to punishment; punishable.

penal.ety: From Old French peinal, from Medieval Latin penalis, from Latin poenalis, from poena (“punishment”), from Ancient Greek ποινή (poinḗ, “punishment”), from Proto-Indo-European *kʷoynéh₂.

ex.en: The country reformed its penal system.
ex.ja: その国は刑罰制度を改革した。

note.ja: ラテン語 poena（罰）から。「刑罰の」。penalty、pain と同じ。

en: One of the component parts of the corolla of a flower. It applies particularly, but not necessarily only, when the corolla consists of se…
The labia (majora).
To spread out from, like the petals of a flower

petal.ety:

Proto-Indo-European *pet-der.
Proto-Hellenic *pétalos
Ancient Greek πέταλον (pétalon)lbor.
English petal
Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek πέταλον (pétalon), from πέταλος (pétalos, “broad, flat”), from Proto-Hellenic *pétalos, from Proto-Indo-European *peth₂- (“to spread out”), whence Latin pandō and Proto-Germanic *faþmaz (“embrace”) (English fathom).

ex.en: Petals lie on the surface of the water.
ex.ja: 花びらが水面に浮かんでいる。

ex.en: The petals of this rose are very tender.
ex.ja: このバラの花びらはとても柔らかい。

ex.en: The petals are floating on the water.
ex.ja: 花びらが水面に浮かんでいる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 petalon（葉）から。petalos（広がった）。「花びら」。

ja: プランク（体幹トレーニング）

en: A flat piece of wood on which to cook fish, so that the wood provides flavor and helps to produce a pleasing texture.
An object made of planks; planking.
To cover something with planking.
To bake (fish, etc.) on a piece of cedar lumber.

plank.ety: From Middle English plank, planke, borrowed from Old French planke, Old Northern French planque (compare French planche, from Old French planche), from Vulgar Latin planca, from palanca, from Latin phalanga. The Latin term derives from the Ancient Greek φάλαγξ (phálanx), so it is thus a doublet of phalange and phalanx. Compare also the doublets planch, planche, and plancha, borrowed later from Middle French, Modern French, and Spanish, respectively.

ex.en: The plank froze to the ground.
ex.ja: 板は地面に凍りついた。

ex.en: He hammered nails into the plank.
ex.ja: 板にくぎを打ち込んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 planca（厚板）から。「厚板」→ 政策の土台の板 →「政策の柱」。

en: A dire or unfortunate situation.
Specifically, to pledge (one's troth etc.) as part of a marriage ceremony.
To promise (oneself) to someone, or to do something.

plight.ety: From Middle English plit (“fold, wrinkle, bad situation”), conflation of Middle English pliht, plight (“risky promise, peril”) (from Old English pliht "danger, risk"; see Etymology 2) and Anglo-Norman plit, plyte (“fold, condition”), from Old French pleit (“condition, manner of folding”) (from Vulgar Latin *plictum, from Latin plicitum (“fold”)).

ex.en: The film shows the plight of refugees.
ex.ja: その映画は難民の苦境を描いている。

note.ja: アングロ・フランス語 plit（状態）から。「（悪い）状態」→「苦境」。

en: The period after the end of the normal sports season during which extra games are held (such as playoffs or championships).
Of or pertaining to such a period.

ex.ja: そのチームはポストシーズン進出を目指している。

en: Having authority over; vested with the authority to preside over.

ex.en: The presiding judge sentenced the defendant to death.
ex.ja: 裁判長は被告に死刑の判決を言い渡した。

ex.en: The presiding judge was touched by pity for the accused.
ex.ja: 裁判長は被告に大いに同情していた。

note.ja: preside（主宰する）+ -ing。prae（前に）+ sedere（座る）。「前に座る」→「議長を務める」。president と同じ。

ja: （privy to で）内々に知っている

en: Private, exclusive; not public; one's own.
With knowledge of; party to; let in on.
An outdoor facility for urination and defecation, whether open (latrine) or enclosed (outhouse).
A lavatory: a room with a toilet.

privy.ety: From Middle English pryvy, prive, from Old French privé (“private”), from Latin prīvātus (“deprived”), perfect passive participle of prīvō (“to bereave, deprive; to free, release”). Doublet of private.

ex.en: Only a few people were privy to the secret.
ex.ja: その秘密を知っていたのはごく一部の人だけだった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 privé（私的な）から。privy to（内々に知っている）→ 古くは「便所」も。private と同じ。

en: The process of propelling, driving, or pushing, typically forward or onward; a propulsive force or impulse.
That which propels.

propulsion.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin propulsio, propulsionis, from the past participle of Latin propello (“to drive forward, drive forth, drive away, drive out”).

ex.en: The rocket uses a new propulsion system.
ex.ja: そのロケットは新しい推進システムを使っている。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ puls（押す）+ ion。前へ押し出すこと →「推進（力）」。propel（推進する）。

en: A flat-bottomed craft able to float and drift on water, used for transport or as a waterborne platform.
Any flattish thing, usually wooden, used in a similar fashion.
To convey on a raft.
To make into a raft.

raft.ety: Late Middle English, of North Germanic origin, from West Old Norse raptr, from Proto-Germanic *raf-tra-, from Proto-Indo-European *rap-tro-, from *rep- (“stake, beam”). See also Norwegian raft (“beam, rafter”), Danish raft (“thin pole”). Compare also Albanian trap (“raft, ferry”).

ex.en: Tom went down the river on a raft.
ex.ja: トムは、いかだで川を下った。

ex.en: The boys went down the river on a raft.
ex.ja: 少年たちはいかだで川をくだった。

ex.en: It was an adventure going down the river on a raft.
ex.ja: いかだでその川を下ったときはハラハラした。

note.ja: 北欧語 raptr（丸太）から。「いかだ」。「大量（a raft of）」は別系統とされる。

en: To be very happy, be delighted, exult; to feel joy.
To make happy, exhilarate.

rejoice.ety: From Middle English rejoicen, rejoisen, from Old French resjoir. Doublet of rejoy. Compare French réjouir; Spanish regocijar; Portuguese regozijar; Italian gioire

ex.en: They rejoiced when they heard he was safe.
ex.ja: 彼が無事だと聞いて彼らは喜んだ。

ex.en: They rejoiced over the news of our success.
ex.ja: 彼らは我々の成功の知らせを喜んだ。

ex.en: We have rejoiced over his discovery.
ex.ja: 私たちは彼の発見を喜んだ。

note.ja: re（強意）+ joir（喜ぶ）。ラテン語 gaudere（喜ぶ）。joy と同じ。

en: That which remains; that which is left after loss or decay; a remaining portion.
Something old and outdated, possibly kept for sentimental reasons.
To cause (an object) to appear old or worn, to distress.
Pertaining to the Big Bang.

relic.ety: From Middle English relik et al., from Old French relique, from Latin reliquiae (“remains, relics”), from relinquō (“to leave behind, abandon, relinquish”), from re- + linquō (“to leave, quit, forsake, depart from”). Doublet of relict, derelict, and relinquish.

ex.en: We discovered relics of an ancient civilization.
ex.ja: 我々は古代文明の遺跡を発見した。

ex.en: Here were some relics.
ex.ja: ここにいくつかの遺跡がありました。

ex.en: Rome abounds with relics.
ex.ja: ローマは至る所に遺跡がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 reliquiae（残り物）から。re + linquere（残す）。「遺物・遺品」。relinquish（放棄する）と同じ。

en: To wander or travel freely and with no specific destination.
To range or wander over.
The act of roaming; a wander; a travel without aim or destination

roam.ety: From Middle English romen, from Old English rāmian, from Proto-Germanic *raimōną (“to wander”), from *raim- (“to move, raise”), from *h₃reyH- (“to move, lift, flow”). Akin to Old English ārǣman (“to arise, stand up, lift up”), Old High German rāmēn (“to aim”) ( > archaic German rahmen (“to strive”)), Middle Dutch rammen (“to night-wander, to copulate”), rammelen (“to wander about, ramble”). More at ramble.

ex.en: I like to roam about the fields.
ex.ja: 私は野原を歩き回るのが好きだ。

ex.en: His eyes roamed over the lake in the valley.
ex.ja: 彼の目は谷間の湖上をずっとさまよった。

ex.en: They roamed about the forest.
ex.ja: 彼らは森を歩き回った。

note.ja: 中英語 romen から。語源ははっきりしない。「歩き回る」。roaming。

en: A type of open shoe made up of straps or bands holding a sole to the foot
To put on sandals.

sandal.ety: From Middle English sandal (“sandal”), from Old French sandale, from Latin sandalium, from Ancient Greek σανδάλιον (sandálion), diminutive of σάνδαλον (sándalon, “sandal”), of unknown origin. Often mistakenly parsed as related to sand.

ex.en: I bought a pair of sandals that match him.
ex.ja: 彼とお揃いのサンダルを買ったの。

ex.en: I bought a pair of sandals.
ex.ja: サンダルを買った。

ex.en: I forgot to bring sandals.
ex.ja: サンダル、持ってくるの忘れちゃった。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 sandalon から。ペルシャ語に由来するとされる。

en: A snake-like creature, such as a sea serpent.
A person who is subtle, malicious, treacherous, or deceiving.

serpent.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *sérpeti

English serpent
From Middle English serpent, from Old French serpent (“snake, serpent”), from Latin serpēns (“snake”), present active participle of serpere (“to creep, crawl”), from Proto-Italic *serpō, from Proto-Indo-European *serp-. In this sense, displaced native Old English nǣdre (“snake, serpent”), whence Modern English adder.
Compare Sanskrit सर्प (sarpa, “snake”), which is a descendant of the same Proto-Indo-European word as

ex.en: In the story, a giant serpent guards the treasure.
ex.ja: その物語では、巨大なヘビが宝を守っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 serpens（這うもの）から。serpere（這う）。「大きなヘビ」。

en: A tropical Asian plant (Sesamum indicum) bearing small flat seeds used as food and as a source of oil.
The seed of this plant.

sesame.ety: From late Middle English sisamie, from Latin sīsamum, sēsamum, from Ancient Greek σήσαμον (sḗsamon), from Aramaic שושמא (šūššmā), shortening of שומשומא (šumššumā), from Akkadian 𒊭𒈦𒌑𒈬 (šamaššammū, “oil plant”), compound of 𒉌𒄑 (šaman, “oil”) and 𒌑 (šammum, “plant”). The modern pronunciation is perhaps influenced by (transliterations of) Greek σησάμη (sisámi). Doublet of sesamum.

ex.en: I want to eat a black sesame ice cream.
ex.ja: 黒ごまのアイスクリームを食べたいよ。

ex.en: I ate black sesame ice cream.
ex.ja: 僕は黒ゴマのアイスクリームを食べました。

ex.en: I want to know how to make black sesame tofu.
ex.ja: 黒ごま豆腐の作り方が知りたい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 sēsamon から。セム語系の言葉に由来する。Open sesame（開けゴマ）は『アラビアンナイト』から。

en: To push, especially roughly or with force.
To move off or along by an act of pushing, as with an oar or pole used in a boat; sometimes with off.
A rough push.
A forward movement of packed river-ice.

shove.ety:
From Middle English schouven, from Old English sċūfan, from Proto-West Germanic *skeuban, from Proto-Germanic *skeubaną, from Proto-Indo-European *skewbʰ-.
See also West Frisian skowe, Low German schuven, Dutch schuiven, German schieben, Danish skubbe, Norwegian Bokmål skyve, Norwegian Nynorsk skuva; also Lithuanian skùbti (“to hurry”), Polish skubać (“to pluck”), Albanian humb (“to lose”).

ex.en: He shoved the letter into his pocket.
ex.ja: 彼は手紙をポケットにねじ込んだ。

ex.en: The man shoved her aside.
ex.ja: その男は彼女を押しのけた。

ex.en: I shoved my hands into my pockets.
ex.ja: 私はポケットに手を突っ込んだ。

note.ja: 古英語 scūfan（押す）から。shovel と同系。「乱暴に押す」。

en: To make simpler, either by reducing in complexity, reducing to component parts, or making easier to understand.
To become simpler.

simplify.ety: From the French simplifier, equivalent to simple + -ify.

ex.en: A good writer needs to be able to simplify complicated things.
ex.ja: 優れた作家は、複雑なものを単純化できる必要があるのです。

note.ja: simpl（単純な）+ ify（〜にする）。単純にする →「簡単にする・単純化する」。

ja: （ギリシャ神話の）セイレーン

en: One of a group of nymphs who lured mariners to their death on the rocks.
One who sings sweetly and charms.
To make a noise with, or as if with, a siren.
To drive with a siren on.
Relating to or like a siren.

siren.ety: From Middle English siren, from Old French sereine and Latin Sīrēn, Sīrēna, from Ancient Greek Σειρήν (Seirḗn). The mammalian sense was first attested in French in Dominique Bouhours, Les entretiens d'Ariste et d'Eugène, in 1671. The aquatic salamander sense was originally introduced by Linnaeus in 1766, for a genus of his reptiles.

ex.en: I heard sirens in the distance.
ex.ja: 遠くにあるサイレンの音が聞こえてきた。

ex.en: I heard a siren.
ex.ja: サイレンが聞こえてきた。

ex.en: The siren sounded an emergency.
ex.ja: サイレンが急変を知らせました。

note.ja: ギリシャ神話で歌声で船乗りを惑わすセイレーン（Seirēn）から。人を引きつける音 →「サイレン」。

ja: （ヒット作に化けた）意外な作品

en: Someone who sleeps.
That which lies dormant, as a law.

sleeper.ety: From Middle English sleper, equivalent to sleep + -er.

ex.en: I'm a light sleeper.
ex.ja: 眠りが浅いんだ。

ex.en: As one grows old, one becomes a light sleeper.
ex.ja: 年を取ると目ざとくなる。

note.ja: sleep + -er。「眠る人・寝台車」→ 遅れてヒットする「意外な作品」。

en: To spread (a substance, especially one that colours or is dirty) across a surface by rubbing.
To cover (a surface with a layer of some substance) by rubbing.
A mark made by smearing.
A presentation of a sauce, purée or other food item, which is placed in a dollop and spread across the plate.

smear.ety:
From Middle English smeren, smerien, from Old English smerian, smyrian, smierwan (“to anoint or rub with grease, oil, etc.”), from Proto-West Germanic *smirwijan, from Proto-Germanic *smirwijaną. Doublet of schmear.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian smeere, Dutch smeren (“to smear, lubricate”), Low German smeren, German schmieren (“to smear, lubricate”), Danish and Norwegian Bokmål smøre (“to lubricate”), Norwegian Nynorsk smørja (“to lubricate”), Swedish smörja (“to grease”), Faroese and Icelandic smyrja.

ex.en: The ruling party is running a smear campaign against the opposition.
ex.ja: 与党は野党非難のキャンペーンを展開しています。

note.ja: 古英語 smierwan（油を塗る）から。「塗りつける」→（評判を）汚す →「中傷する」。

en: Marked by snow; characterized by snow.
Covered with snow; snow-covered; besnowed.
Synonym of snowy owl.
Synonym of snowy egret.

snowy.ety: From Middle English snowy, snawy; from Old English snāwiġ. By surface analysis, snow + -y.

ex.en: As the weather was snowy, we went skiing.
ex.ja: 雪の降る天気だったので、私たちはスキーに行った。

ex.en: It's a snowy day.
ex.ja: 雪降りの日です。

ex.en: According to the weather forecast, tomorrow will be snowy.
ex.ja: 天気予報によればあすは雪だ。

note.ja: snow + -y。「雪の多い」。

en: Of, or pertaining to, spectres; ghostly.

ex.en: A spectral figure appeared in the mist.
ex.ja: 霧の中に幽霊のような姿が現れた。

note.ja: spectrum（スペクトル）・specter（幽霊）+ -al。ラテン語 specere（見る）。「見えるもの」から両方の意味。

ex.en: Australians are, on the whole, pleased with the stabilizing benefits of their political system.

en: The stem or main axis of a plant.
The petiole, pedicel, or peduncle of a plant.
To approach slowly and quietly in order not to be discovered when getting closer.
To (try to) follow or contact someone constantly, often resulting in harassment.ᵂᵖ

stalk.ety:
From Middle English stalke, stelke, stalk, perhaps from Old English *stealc, *stielc, *stealuc, from Proto-West Germanic *staluk, *stalik, from Proto-Germanic *stalukaz, *stalikaz, diminutive of Proto-Germanic *stalô, *staluz (“support, stem, stalk”), from Proto-Indo-European *stel- (“to place, stand; be stiff; stud, post, trunk, stake, stem, stalk”).

ex.en: The stalk is a little bigger around than your little finger.
ex.ja: その茎は君の小指よりやや太い。

ex.en: Wash the strawberries and remove their stalks.
ex.ja: イチゴを洗って、ヘタを取って。

ex.en: Wolves stalked the flock.
ex.ja: オオカミが羊の群れに忍び寄った。

note.ja: 「茎」は古英語 stela から。「忍び寄る」は古英語 stealcian（こっそり歩く）からで別語、steal と同系。

en: A man who is a leader in national or international affairs.
A male political leader who promotes the public good or who is recognized for probity, leadership, or the qualities necessary to govern a…

statesman.ety: From state + -s- + -man, modelled after French homme d'État.

ex.en: The great statesman and general is still living.
ex.ja: 偉大な政治家でもあり将軍である人はまだ生きている。

ex.en: Statesmen of this kind are hard to find.
ex.ja: こういうタイプの政治家はめったにいない。

ex.en: The newspaper reported the death of the statesman.
ex.ja: 新聞はその政治家の死を報道した。

note.ja: state（国家）+ s + man。「国家の人」→「（立派な）政治家」。

en: To have a strong bad smell.
To be greatly inferior; to perform badly.
A strong bad smell.
A complaint or objection.
Bad-smelling, stinky.

stink.ety:
From Middle English stinken, from Old English stincan, from Proto-Germanic *stinkwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *stengʷ-, *stegʷ- (“to push, thrust, strike”). Cognate with West Frisian stjonke (“to stink”), Dutch stinken (“to stink”), German stinken (“to stink”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, and Norwegian Nynorsk stinke (“to stink”), Swedish stinka (“to stink”), Icelandic stökkva (“to spring, leap, jump”).
Compare typologically Russian рази́ть (razítʹ).

ex.en: I'll bid farewell to this stinking school.
ex.ja: このひどい学校にはおさらばだ。

ex.en: Durian stinks, but it's said to be very healthy.
ex.ja: ドリアンは臭いけど、体にはとてもいいと言われています。

ex.en: He is raising a big stink over a minor glitch.
ex.ja: 彼はささいな故障に大騒ぎをしています。

note.ja: 古英語 stincan（においがする）から。「悪臭を放つ」。stench と同じ。

en: Of or pertaining to storms.
Characterized by, or proceeding from, a storm; subject to storms; agitated with strong winds and heavy rain.

stormy.ety: From Middle English stormy, stormi, from Old English *stormiġ (“stormy”), equivalent to storm + -y. Cognate with Dutch stormig (“stormy”), German stürmisch (“stormy”), Swedish stormig (“stormy”).

ex.en: I hope this stormy weather won't go on.
ex.ja: この嵐が続かなければいいのですが。

ex.en: There is no going out in this stormy weather.
ex.ja: こんな悪天候では外出できない。

ex.en: It was stormy the day before yesterday.
ex.ja: おとといは嵐だった。

note.ja: storm（嵐）+ -y。「嵐の・激しい」。

en: To be enough or sufficient; to meet the need (of anything); to be adequate; to be good enough.
To satisfy; to content; to be equal to the wants or demands of.

suffice.ety: From Middle English suffisen, from Middle French souffire, from Latin sufficiō (“supply, be adequate”), from sub (“under”) + faciō (“do, make”). Cognate with French suffire.

ex.ja: 結局これでは駄目だとだけ言っておこう。

ex.en: That will suffice for now.
ex.ja: 今のところそれで間に合うでしょう。

note.ja: suf（下から）+ fic（作る・する）+ e。下から満たす →「十分である」。sufficient（十分な）。

en: A pig, an animal of family Suidae, especially in agricultural contexts.
Pig, pork, the meat of pigs.

swine.ety:
From Middle English swyn, swin; from Old English swīn; from Proto-West Germanic *swīn; from Proto-Germanic *swīną; from an adjectival form of Proto-Indo-European *suH- (“pig”).
* In modern use, especially as a term of abuse, frequently a calque of German Schwein or its derivatives.
* In reference to wolffish, a clipping of swinefish.
Cognates
Related to West Frisian swyn, Low German Swien, Dutch zwijn, German Schwein, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish svin, Faroese and Icelandic svín, and more distantly to Polish świnia, Russian свинья́ (svinʹjá), Latin sūinus, Latin sūs

ex.en: Don't cast pearls before swine.
ex.ja: 豚の前に真珠を投げ与えるな。

note.ja: 古英語 swīn から。sow（雌豚）と同系。swine flu（豚インフルエンザ）。

An art movement originating in late 19th-century France and Belgium, seeking to represent absolute truths symbolically through language a…

note.ja: symbol（象徴）+ -ism。「象徴性・象徴主義」。

Intricate.

ex.ja: 赤ん坊が毛糸の玉をもつれさせた。

ex.en: The threads got tangled.
ex.ja: 糸が絡まった。

note.ja: tangle（もつれさせる）+ -ed。「もつれた」。

en: A passenger vehicle for public use that runs on tracks in the road (called a streetcar or trolley in North America).
A similar vehicle for carrying materials.
To operate, or conduct the business of, a tramway.
To travel by tram.

tram.ety:
Early 16th century, borrowed from Scots, probably from Low German traam (“tram, shaft of a barrow”), from Middle Low German and Middle Dutch trame (“narrow shaft, beam”), said to be ultimately from a lost West Germanic (Ingvaeonic) word, probably from Proto-Germanic *drum (“splinter, fragment”), from Proto-Indo-European *térmn̥ (“peg, post, boundary”), cognate with Latin terminus.
Compare Middle Low German treme; West Flemish traam, trame.
The popular derivation from the surname of the English pioneer tramway builder Benjamin Outram (1764–1805) is false: the term pre-dated him.
The sense of a

note.ja: 中世低地ドイツ語 trame（梁・板）から。鉱山のトロッコのレール →「路面電車」。

en: Physically strong and active.
Mentally strong and active.

vigorous.ety: From Anglo-Norman vigrus, from Old French vigoros (French vigoureux), from Medieval Latin vigorosus, from Latin vigor. Doublet of vigoroso.

ex.ja: 私たちは活発な討論をした。

note.ja: vigor（活力）+ -ous。ラテン語 vigere（元気である）。「活発な」。

en: In violation of a moral or other standard, code, or convention; in an unfair, unjust, dishonest, or immoral manner; wrongly convicted is …
Incorrectly, mistakenly; by error.

wrongly.ety: From Middle English wrongly, wrongliche, equivalent to wrong + -ly.

ex.en: Having been wrongly addressed, the letter never reached him.
ex.ja: 宛名が違っていたので、その手紙は彼の所に届かなかった。

ex.en: Mary was wrongly imprisoned for nearly 10 years.
ex.ja: メアリーは、10年近くの間、不当に投獄されていました。

note.ja: wrong + -ly。「誤って」。

en: Indicating delight at the flavor of food.
Indicating delight in other things.
Delicious.

ex.ja: 「おいしい！このケーキ最高！」

note.ja: おいしいときの擬声語。

en: Belief that no deities exist (sometimes including rejection of other religious beliefs).
A lack of belief in deities, or a belief that there is insufficient evidence to believe in a god.

atheism.ety:
16th century Middle French athéisme, from athée (“atheist”), a loan from Ancient Greek ἄθεος (átheos, “godless”, from ἀ- (a-, “without”) + θεός (theós, “deity, god”)).
First English attestation dates to 1587 (OED).

ex.en: Socrates was accused of atheism because he did not believe in Zeus.
ex.ja: ソクラテスは主神ゼウスを信じなかったので無神論の罪に問われた。

note.ja: a（否定）+ the（神）+ ism。神を認めない主義 →「無神論」。

en: Able to be heard.
To change the play at the line of scrimmage by yelling out a new one.
The act of or an instance of changing the play at the line of scrimmage by yelling out a new one.

audible.ety: Borrowed from Middle French audible, from Late Latin audibilis, from Latin audire (“to hear”).

ex.en: Airplanes are audible long before they are visible.
ex.ja: 飛行機は姿の見えるずっと前から音が聞こえる。

note.ja: aud（聞く）+ ible（〜できる）。聞くことができる →「聞こえる」。inaudible（聞こえない）。

en: The large, usually yellowish-green or black, savory fruit of the avocado tree.
The avocado tree, Persea americana, of the laurel family.
Of a dull yellowish-green colour.

avocado.ety:
Borrowed from Latin American Spanish avocado, from the earlier aguacate, which comes from Classical Nahuatl āhuacatl (“avocado”). Doublet of abacate. Compare aguacatillo, avocadillo.
The first mention can be found in a catalogue of Jamaican plants in 1696.

ex.en: Avocados are rich in vitamin E.
ex.ja: アボカドはビタミンＥが豊富です。

ex.en: The avocado is rich in nutrients.
ex.ja: アボカドは栄養豊富です。

ex.en: The avocado is rich in fats.
ex.ja: アボカドには脂肪分が豊富に含まれています。

note.ja: スペイン語 aguacate の変化形。ナワトル語（アステカの言語）āhuacatl に由来する。

en: A large container for holding water in which a person may bathe (take a bath).

ex.en: He has the water running in the bathtub.
ex.ja: 彼は浴槽に水を出しっぱなしにしている。

ex.en: Tom filled the bathtub up with hot water.
ex.ja: トムはお風呂を入れた。

ex.en: He likes to sing in the bathtub.
ex.ja: 彼はお風呂で歌うのが好きだ。

note.ja: bath（風呂）+ tub（おけ）。「浴槽」。

en: The sound produced by the horn of a car, or any similar sound.
A short, electronically produced tone.
To produce a beep sound.
To have sexual intercourse with (someone), referring to the bleep tone used to censor obscene words in broadcasts.

ex.en: Leave your message after hearing the beep.
ex.ja: 発信音が聞こえた後であなたのメッセージを残してください。

ex.en: Did you hear your computer beep?

ex.ja: ただいま留守にしております。ピーッという音が鳴りましたら、ご用件をお話しください。

note.ja: 擬音語。「ピー」。

en: One who benefits or receives an advantage.
One who benefits from the distribution, especially out of a trust or estate.
Holding some office or valuable possession, in subordination to another; holding under a feudal or other superior; having a dependent and…
Bestowed as a gratuity.

beneficiary.ety: From Latin beneficiarius (“enjoying a favor, granted a privilege”) from beneficium (“benefit”), perhaps via or influenced by French bénéficiaire (“beneficiary”). Indirectly, by way of the etymology of the Latin word beneficium, the English word beneficiary ultimately has the same origin as the English word benefactor, its near antonym.

ex.en: She is the sole beneficiary of the insurance.
ex.ja: 彼女はその保険の唯一の受取人だ。

note.ja: benefit + -iary。「利益を受ける人」→「受益者・受取人」。

en: The quality of having a bitter taste.
The quality of feeling bitter; acrimony, resentment; the quality of exhibiting such feelings.

bitterness.ety: From Middle English bitternesse, biternesse, from Old English biternes (“bitterness; grief”), equivalent to bitter + -ness.

ex.en: I can't look at this photograph without bitterness.
ex.ja: この写真を見る度に、心が痛みます。

note.ja: bitter（苦い）+ -ness。「苦さ・恨み」。bitter は bite（かむ）と同じ祖先。

en: Obvious, on show; unashamed; loudly obtrusive or offensive.

blatant.ety:
Coined by Edmund Spenser in 1596 in "blatant beast". Probably a variation of *blatand (Scots blaitand (“bleating”)), present participle of blate, a variation of bleat, equivalent to blate + -ant. See bleat. In addition, it is suggested by Latin blatiō (“speak like a fool, prate”), which is rare, and so the similitude may be just coincidental.
Compare typologically Bulgarian вопиющ (vopijušt), Russian вопию́щий (vopijúščij) (akin to вопи́ть (vopítʹ)).

ex.en: I glared at him with a blatant look of disapproval on my face.
ex.ja: 露骨に嫌な顔をして、彼を睨みつけた。

note.ja: 16世紀の詩人スペンサーの造語とされる。「騒々しい」→「あからさまな」。

en: A good thing; a thing to be thankful for or to appreciate duly.
That which is asked or granted as a benefit or favor; a gift or benefaction.
Gay; merry; jovial; convivial.

boon.ety: From Middle English boon (“prayer”), from Old Norse bón (“prayer, petition”), from Proto-Germanic *bōniz (“supplication”), influenced by boon (“good, favorable”, adjective). Doublet of ben; see there for more.

ex.en: The new train line has been a boon to local businesses.
ex.ja: 新しい鉄道路線は地元の商店にとって恩恵となった。

note.ja: 古北欧語 bón（頼み）から。「（願いに応えた）恩恵」。

A rough cloak or ragged garment.
To act in a bratty manner as the submissive.
Characteristic of a confident and assertive woman.

To provide a bunk.

To hold or grip tightly.

ex.ja: さっそく矛盾が出てきてる。

ex.en: His voting record is riddled with contradictions.
ex.ja: 彼の票決記録をたどると矛盾だらけです。

note.ja: contra（反対に）+ dict（言う）+ ion。反対のことを言うこと →「矛盾・反論」。

en: An act of investing with a crown; a crowning.
An act or the ceremony of formally investing a sovereign or the sovereign's consort with a crown and other insignia of royalty, on or sho…

coronation.ety: From Late Middle English coronacion, coronacioun (“crowning of a sovereign or his consort; powers conferred by this ceremony; crowning of the Virgin Mary; (figuratively) placing of a crown of thorns on Jesus; act of rewarding a person with eternal life, happiness, honour, etc.”) [and other forms], borrowed from Anglo-Norman coronacion and Old French coronacion, coronation, from Late Latin *corōnātiōnem, from Latin corōnō (“to coronate, crown (with a crown, garland, etc.)”) + -ātiōnem (suffix forming nouns relating to actions or their results). Corōnō is derived from corōna (“garland, wreath; c

ex.en: The coronation of the new king took place in May.
ex.ja: 新しい国王の戴冠式は５月に行われた。

note.ja: ラテン語 coronare（冠をかぶせる）から。corona（冠）。「戴冠式」。crown と同じ語源。

en: A dry, thin, crispy baked bread (usually salty or savoury, but sometimes sweet, as in the case of graham crackers and animal crackers).
A prawn cracker.

cracker.ety:
From Middle English craker (“a boaster”), equivalent to crack (“to break, snap, utter, make a sound”) + -er. From crack (verb), the sound made when one is broken. The hard "bread" and "biscuit" sense is first attested in 1739.
The computing senses of cracker, crack, and cracking were promoted in the 1980s as an alternative to hacker, by programmers concerned about negative public associations of hack, hacking (“creative computer coding”). See Citations:cracker.
Various theories exist regarding the term's application to poor white Southerners. One theory holds that it originated with disadvanta

ex.en: He lived on crackers and water for three days.
ex.ja: 彼はビスケットと水で三日間命をつないだ。

ex.en: Mum, the rice crackers have gone soft and they don't taste good anymore.
ex.ja: お母さん、このおせんべい、しけってておいしくないよ。

ex.en: Mum, the rice crackers have gotten damp and they're not nice anymore.
ex.ja: お母さん、このおせんべい、しけってておいしくないよ。

note.ja: crack（パリッと割れる）+ -er。「パリッとしたもの」→「クラッカー・爆竹」。

en: Sly; crafty; clever in surreptitious behaviour.
Practical knowledge or experience; aptitude in performance; skill, proficiency; dexterity.
Practical skill employed in a secret or crafty manner; craft; artifice; skillful deceit; art or magic.

cunning.ety: From Middle English cunning, kunning, konnyng, alteration of earlier Middle English cunninde, kunnende, cunnand, from Old English cunnende, present participle of cunnan (“to know how to, be able to”), equivalent to con + -ing. Cognate with Scots cunnand (“cunning”), German könnend (“able to do”), Icelandic kunnandi (“cunning”). More at con, can.

ex.en: People say that the fox is more cunning than other animals.
ex.ja: キツネは他の動物よりずる賢いと言われています。

ex.en: I see Tom as cunning rather than clever.
ex.ja: トムは賢いというよりずる賢いイメージだな。

ex.en: It is said that the fox is more cunning than any other animal.
ex.ja: 狐は他のどんな動物よりもずるいということだ。

note.ja: 古英語 cunnan（知っている）から。can と同じ祖先。「知恵がある」→「ずる賢い」。

en: A lifelike image of something, either verbal or visual.
A drawing or painting.

depiction.ety: From French dépiction, from Latin dēpictiō. By surface analysis, depict + -ion.

ex.en: Dickens' thoughts come across along with the vivid depiction of old London.
ex.ja: ディッケンズの考えが、ロンドンの下町の生き生きした描写と共に読者には伝わる。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ pict（描く）+ ion。描き出すこと →「描写」。depict（描写する）。

en: Used up, expended; of which nothing is left.

ex.en: The country's oil reserves are almost depleted.
ex.ja: その国の石油埋蔵量はほとんど枯渇している。

note.ja: deplete（使い果たす）+ -ed。de + plere（満たす）。「満たしたものを抜く」→「枯渇した」。complete と同じ ple。

en: Of or pertaining to diabetes, especially diabetes mellitus.
Having diabetes, especially diabetes mellitus.
A person with diabetes, usually diabetes mellitus.

ex.en: My uncle is diabetic and watches what he eats.
ex.ja: おじは糖尿病なので食べるものに気をつけている。

note.ja: diabetes + -ic。「糖尿病の」。

en: The dispersion of a group in a manner comparable to that of the Jews among the Gentiles after the Babylonian captivity (6th century BCE).
Jews outside of the land of Israel.

diaspora.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek διασπορᾱ́ (diasporā́, “dispersion”), from διασπείρω (diaspeírō, “to scatter”), from δια- (dia-, prefix indicating motion across or in all directions) + σπείρω (speírō, “to sow”).

ex.en: The Irish diaspora is spread all over the world.
ex.ja: アイルランド系の人々は世界中に散らばっている。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diaspora（散らばること）から。dia（あちこちに）+ speirein（種をまく）。「離散」。sperm と同じ。

ex.en: The old photos were digitally restored.
ex.ja: 古い写真はデジタルで修復された。

en: Lack of concord, agreement, harmony; disaccord.
Tension or strife resulting from a lack of agreement; dissension.

discord.ety:
Circa 1230, Middle English descorde, discorde; from Anglo-Norman, Old French descort (derivative of descorder), descorde (“disagreement”); from Latin discordia, from discors (“disagreeing, disagreement”), from dis- (“apart”) + cor, cordis (“heart”).
Verb derives from Middle English discorden, from Anglo-Norman, Old French descorder, from Latin discordāre, from discord-, as above.

ex.en: Finally, the discord between them came to an end.
ex.ja: ついに両者の間の不和は終わりになった。

ex.en: A gift of cheesecake is apparently good to soothe discord.
ex.ja: 波風を鎮めるにはチーズケーキのお土産が良いらしいですよ。

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ cord（心）。心が離れること →「不一致・不和・不協和音」。

en: The state, position, or fact of being a god or God.
Synonym of deity.

divinity.ety: From Old French divinité, from Latin divinitas. Composed of divine + -ity. Displaced native Old English godcundnes.

ex.en: He studied divinity at Oxford.
ex.ja: 彼はオックスフォード大学で神学を学んだ。

note.ja: divine（神の）+ -ity。ラテン語 divus（神の）。「神性・神学」。deity と同系。

ex.ja: 1ダースのドーナッツを買いたいです。

ex.ja: トムは、コーヒーとドーナツを頼んでたよ。

ex.en: I'd like to buy a dozen donuts.
ex.ja: 1ダースのドーナッツを買いたいです。

note.ja: doughnut の短縮。dough（生地）+ nut（木の実）。小さな丸い揚げ菓子だったことから。

en: Relating to the top surface of the foot or hand.
Produced using the dorsum of the tongue.
A hanging, usually of rich stuff, at the back of a throne, altar, etc.
Any of the longitudinal series of plates that encircle the body, excluding the ventral scales.

dorsal.ety: From Late Middle English dorsal/dorsale, borrowing from Medieval Latin dorsālis (“of or relating to the back”), from dorsum (“the back”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix); equivalent to dorsum + -al.

ex.en: We saw the dolphin's dorsal fin.
ex.ja: イルカの背びれが見えた。

note.ja: ラテン語 dorsum（背）から。dorsal fin（背びれ）。

en: The ability to last a long time by virtue of the power to resist stress or force.

durability.ety: From Middle English durabilite, from Old French durabilité, from Latin dūrābilitās (“durability”). Corresponding to durable + -ity.

ex.en: He checked the durability of the house before buying it.
ex.ja: 彼は家の耐久性を買う前に調べた。

ex.en: This machine is inferior to that one in durability.
ex.ja: この機械は、耐久性であの機械に劣ります。

note.ja: dur（続く）+ ability。長く続く性質 →「耐久性」。

en: British standard spelling of endeavor.
British standard spelling of endeavor.

ex.en: We will endeavour to answer all your questions.
ex.ja: すべてのご質問にお答えするよう努めます。

note.ja: endeavor のイギリスのつづり。en + devoir（義務）。「努力」。

en: To enter (a name, etc.) in a register, roll or list
To enlist (someone) or make (someone) a member of.

enroll.ety: From Middle English enrollen, from Anglo-Norman enroller; by surface analysis, en- + roll.

ex.en: He was not allowed to enroll in the college.
ex.ja: 彼はその大学に入学を許可されなかった。

ex.en: They enrolled him as a jury member.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼を陪審員として登録した。

ex.en: He is enrolled at that university.
ex.ja: 彼はその大学に在学している。

note.ja: en（中に）+ roll（名簿）。「名簿に載せる」→「入学する・登録する」。enrol のアメリカのつづり。

Someone who puts on a show for the entertainment or enjoyment of others.

ex.ja: 彼は芸人として成功した。

note.ja: entertain（楽しませる）+ -er。inter（間に）+ tenere（保つ）。「人の注意をつなぎとめる人」。

ex.ja: そのお仕事、お任せしてもよろしいでしょうか。

ex.en: I entrusted my property to the lawyer.
ex.ja: 私は自分の財産を弁護士に委ねた。

ex.en: She entrusted her husband with a letter.
ex.ja: 彼女は夫に手紙を預けた。

note.ja: en（中に）+ trust（信頼）。「信頼して任せる」。

en: The state proceeding from destiny; invincible necessity, superior to, and independent of, free and rational control.
Tendency to death, destruction or danger, as if by decree of fate.

fatality.ety: From French fatalité. equivalent to fatal + -ity. The video game move sense was popularized by the Mortal Kombat series.

ex.en: The accident caused one fatality.
ex.ja: その事故で一人が死亡した。

note.ja: fatal（致命的な）+ -ity。ラテン語 fatum（運命・死）。「死亡事故・死者」。fate と同じ。

en: A festival or similar celebration.
An experience or expression of celebratory feeling, merriment, gaiety.

festivity.ety: Inherited from Middle English festivite, from Middle French festivité, from Latin festīvitas, equivalent to festive + -ity.

ex.en: The festivities were held as usual this year.
ex.ja: お祭りは今年も例年通り開催された。

note.ja: festive + -ity。「お祝い」→（festivities）祝祭行事。

en: A utensil with spikes used to put solid food into the mouth, or to hold food down while cutting, or for serving food.
Any of several types of pronged tools for use on farms, in fields, or in the garden or lawn, such as a smaller hand fork for weeding or a…
To divide into two or more branches or copies.
To spawn a new child process by duplicating the existing process.

fork.ety: From Middle English forke (“digging fork”), from Old English force, forca (“forked instrument used to torture”), from Proto-West Germanic *furkō (“fork”), from Latin furca (“pitchfork, forked stake; gallows, beam, stake, support post, yoke”), of uncertain origin. The Middle English word was later reinforced by Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French forque (= Old French forche whence French fourche), also from the Latin. Doublet of fourche and furcate. Cognate also with North Frisian forck (“fork”), Dutch vork (“fork”), Danish fork (“fork”), German Forke (“pitchfork”). Displaced native gafol, ġeafel

ex.en: I took the right fork of the road.
ex.ja: 私は分かれ道を右手に行った。

ex.en: They eat with a knife and fork.
ex.ja: 彼らはナイフとフォークで食事をする。

ex.en: There's a fork in the road here.
ex.ja: 道はここで二つに分かれている。

note.ja: ラテン語 furca（熊手）から。「フォーク・分岐点」。

en: To draw in the breath suddenly, as if from a shock.
To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion; to respire with heaving of the breast; to pant.
A short, sudden intake of breath.
The sound of a gasp.

gasp.ety: From Middle English gaspen, gayspen (“to gape, outbreathe”), related to and likely derived from Old Norse geispa (“to yawn”) or its descendant Danish gispe, which may be related to gapa (“to gape”).

ex.en: He was gasping for breath as he ran.
ex.ja: 彼は息を切らして走り続けた。

ex.en: I ran while gasping for air.
ex.ja: 私は息を切らせて走った。

ex.en: She gasped out the news.
ex.ja: 彼女はその知らせをあえぎながら伝えた。

note.ja: 北欧語 geispa（あくびをする）から。「はっと息をのむ」。

en: Of or relating to biological reproduction.
Of or relating to the genitalia.

genital.ety: From Middle English genital, from Latin genitalis (“of or belonging to generation”), from genitus, past participle of gignō (“to beget, generate”); see genus.

ex.en: The doctor examined the baby for any genital problems.
ex.ja: 医師は赤ちゃんの生殖器に異常がないか診察した。

note.ja: ラテン語 genitalis（生殖の）から。gignere（生む）。gene、generate と同じ。

en: A problem affecting function.
An unexpected behavior in an electrical signal, especially if the signal spontaneously returns to expected behavior after a period of time.
To experience an unexpected, typically intermittent malfunction.
To perform an exploit or recreate a bug while playing a video game.

glitch.ety:
Probably borrowed from Yiddish גליטש (glitsh), from German glitschig (“slippy”), from glitschen (“to slide, glide, slip”) + -ig (“-y”). Related to gleiten (“glide”). Cognate with French glisser (“to slip, slide, skid”).
Popularized in the 1960s, by the US space program. Attested in 1962 by American astronaut John Glenn, in reference to spikes in electrical current.

ex.en: He is raising a big stink over a minor glitch.
ex.ja: 彼はささいな故障に大騒ぎをしています。

note.ja: 1960年代アメリカの語。イディッシュ語 glitsh（滑ること）とされる。「小さな不具合」。

en: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal disk that emits a loud resonant sound when struck with a soft hammer.
A metal target that emits a sound when it has been hit.
To make the sound of a gong; to ring a gong.
To halt (originally, a contestant in a talent show; later, a performer, a speaker).

ex.en: The room emptied when the gong for dinner sounded.
ex.ja: 食事のドラが鳴ると部屋はからになった。

note.ja: マレー語 gong（擬音）から。「どら」。

en: Having a slippery surface; having a surface covered with grease.
Containing a lot of grease or fat.
An annoyed or contemptuous look; a dirty look.
Wool that still contains grease and has not undergone scouring.

greasy.ety: From Middle English gresi, gressy, equivalent to grease + -y.

ex.en: What is that greasy stuff on your shirt?
ex.ja: シャツについている、べとべとしたものは何ですか。

ex.en: I have greasy skin.
ex.ja: 肌が脂っぽいのです。

ex.en: My hair is greasy.
ex.ja: 髪の毛がべとべとしている。

note.ja: grease（油脂）+ -y。「脂っこい」。

en: Feeling or showing sorrow or distress due to loss, especially the death of someone.
An act or instance of feeling or expressing grief.

ex.en: The grieving woman was consoled by her friends.
ex.ja: 悲しみに暮れるその女性は友人たちに慰められた。

ex.en: The mother was still grieving over her child's death.
ex.ja: その母親は子供の死をいまだに嘆き悲しんでいた。

note.ja: grieve（嘆き悲しむ）+ -ing。grief と同じ。

en: A hot sandwich consisting of a patty of cooked ground beef or a meat substitute, in a sliced bun, usually also containing salad vegetable…
The patty used in such a sandwich.
To badly injure or damage (a fleshy part of the body).

hamburger.ety: Shortening of Hamburger sandwich, Hamburger steak, etc., the first element borrowed from German Hamburger (“native of Hamburg”), equivalent to Hamburg + -er.

ex.en: Is it OK if I eat this hamburger?
ex.ja: このハンバーガーを食べてもいいですか。

ex.en: If you're still hungry, have another hamburger.
ex.ja: まだお腹がすいてるんなら、もう１つハンバーガーを食べてね。

ex.en: Boy, that hamburger really hit the spot.
ex.ja: あのハンバーガーは本当においしかった。

note.ja: ドイツの都市ハンブルク（Hamburg）風のステーキから。ham（ハム）とは無関係。

en: Careful attention.
To mind; to regard with care; to take notice of; to attend to; to observe.

heed.ety: From Middle English heden, from Old English hēdan (“to heed, take care, observe, attend, guard, take charge, take possession, receive”), from Proto-West Germanic *hōdijan (“to heed, guard”), from Proto-Indo-European *kadʰ- (“to heed, protect”). Cognate with West Frisian hoedje (“to heed”), Dutch hoeden (“to heed”), German hüten (“to heed”).

ex.en: You must heed the advice of your teacher.
ex.ja: 先生のおっしゃることを注意して聞かなければなりません。

ex.en: The man gave no heed to her loud protest.
ex.ja: その男は彼女が大声で反対するのに耳を貸さなかった。

ex.en: They gave no heed to the warning.
ex.ja: 彼らは警告に全然注意を払わなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 hēdan（気をつける）から。「注意を払う」。heedless（不注意な）。

en: Extremely or shockingly ugly.
Having a very unpleasant or frightening sound.

hideous.ety:
From Middle English hidous, from Anglo-Norman hidous, from Old French hideus, hydus (“that which inspires terror”), from earlier hisdos, from Old French hisda (“horror, fear”), of uncertain and disputed origin. Probably from Proto-West Germanic *agisiþu (“horror, terror”), from Proto-West Germanic *agisōn (“to frighten, terrorise”), from Proto-Germanic *agaz (“terror, fear”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂egʰ- (“to frighten”). Cognate with Old High German egisa, egidī (“horror”), Old English egesa (“fear, dread”), Gothic 𐌰𐌲𐌹𐍃 (agis, “fear, terror”).
Alternative etymology cites possible derivatio

ex.en: A hideous monster used to live there.
ex.ja: 以前恐ろしい怪物が住んでいた。

ex.en: Tom had a hideous hangover.
ex.ja: トムがとんでもない二日酔いをしてしまいました。

note.ja: 古フランス語 hidos（恐ろしい）から。「ひどく醜い」。

en: A circular band of metal used to bind a barrel.
Any circular band or ring.
To bind or fasten using a hoop.
To clasp; to encircle; to surround.

hoop.ety: From Middle English hoop, hoope, from Old English hōp (“mound, raised land; in combination, circular object”), from Proto-Germanic *hōpą (“bend, bow, arch”) (compare Saterland Frisian Houp (“hoop”), Dutch hoep (“hoop”), Old Norse hóp (“bay, inlet”)), from Proto-Indo-European *kāb- (“to bend”) (compare Lithuanian kabė (“hook”), Old Church Slavonic кѫпъ (kǫpŭ, “hill, island”)). More at camp.

ex.en: I'd jump through hoops for you.
ex.ja: 君のためならたとえ火の中水の中。

note.ja: 古英語 hōp（輪）から。「輪・（バスケットの）リング」。

想像力豐富的 /想像力丰富的

en: Having a lively or creative imagination.
Tending to be fanciful or inventive.

imaginative.ety: From Middle English ymagynatif, from Middle French imaginatif, from Medieval Latin imāginātīvus. By surface analysis, imagine + -ative.

ex.en: He used to be an imaginative boy.
ex.ja: 彼は想像力のたくましい少年であった。

ex.en: He is a very imaginative writer.
ex.ja: 彼は非常に想像力にとんだ作家です。

ex.en: This novel is very imaginative.
ex.ja: この小説は想像力に富んでいる。

note.ja: imagine + -ative。「想像力豊かな」。

Unisexual: having either male (with stamens) or female (with pistil) flowers, but not with both.
Something having a minor flaw.
A tense of verbs used in describing a past action that is incomplete or continuous.

ex.ja: 誰にでも欠点はある。それでいいのよ。

ex.en: Partly because he could not receive enough information, Harper's description remains imperfect.
ex.ja: 十分な情報を受け取ることができなかったという理由も一部にはあって、ハーパーの描写は不完全なものにとどまっている。

en: Suggested indirectly, without being directly expressed; Implied.
Contained in the essential nature of something but not openly shown.

implicit.ety: From Middle French implicite, from Latin implicitus, past participle of implico (“to infold, involve, entangle”); see implicate.

ex.en: We had an implicit agreement that we would support each other.
ex.ja: 我々には互いに支持しあおうという暗黙の了解があった。

note.ja: im（中に）+ plic（折る）+ it。中に折り込まれた →「暗黙の・それとなく示された」。explicit（明白な）と対。

en: A body of water let into a coast, such as a bay, cove, fjord or estuary.
A passage that leads into a cavity.
To let in; admit.
To insert; inlay.

inlet.ety: From Middle English inlāte (“inlet, entrance”), from inleten (“to let in”), equivalent to in- + let. Compare Low German inlat (“inlet”), German Einlass (“inlet, entrance”).

ex.en: The boat sailed into a narrow inlet.
ex.ja: ボートは狭い入り江に入っていった。

note.ja: in（中に）+ let（入れる）。「海が入り込んだ所」→「入り江・注入口」。

en: Expressing or feeling little or no concern, care, compassion, or consideration for the feelings, emotions, sentiments, or concerns of oth…
Not expressing normal physical feeling.

insensitive.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Italic *n̥-
Latin in-bor.
Middle English in-
English in-
English sensitive
English insensitive
From in- + sensitive.

ex.en: I think that Tom is insensitive.
ex.ja: トムって無神経だと思う。

ex.en: That person is insensitive, aren't they?
ex.ja: あの人、鈍感よね？

ex.en: I think Tom is insensitive.
ex.ja: トムって無神経だと思う。

note.ja: in（否定）+ sensitive（敏感な）。「無神経な・鈍感な」。

en: A person who lives on an island.

islander.ety: From island + -er. Displaced Middle English insulane (“islander”), from Latin īnsulānus (“islander”).

ex.en: The islanders are asking us for help.
ex.ja: その島の人々は我々の助けを求めている。

ex.en: The islanders are nice.
ex.ja: 島の人たちは、優しいです。

ex.en: The islanders are kind.
ex.ja: 島の人たちは、優しいです。

note.ja: island（島）+ -er。「島民」。island の s は isle の影響で綴りに入った。

en: The top stone of an arch.
Something on which other things depend for support.
To distort (an image) by projecting it onto a surface at an angle, which for example causes a square to look like a trapezoid.
To double the cost price in order to determine the retail price; to apply a markup of 100%.

keystone.ety:
From key + stone.
Definition 4 (retail) possibly originated in the jewelry industry in the magazine called "Jewelers' Circular-Keystone".

ex.en: Trust is the keystone of any relationship.
ex.ja: 信頼はどんな人間関係においても要となるものだ。

note.ja: key（鍵・要）+ stone（石）。アーチの頂上に入れて全体を支える石 →「要石・要」。

en: Praise; accolades.
Credit for one's achievements.
An interjection indicating praise or approval or as an acknowledgement of a laudable achievement.
To give praise or accolades.

kudos.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κῦδος (kûdos, “praise, renown”).

ex.en: Kudos for your outstanding achievement!
ex.ja: 素晴らしい業績に拍手を送ります。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kydos（栄光）から。「称賛」。単数扱い。

ja: （in lieu of で）〜の代わりに

en: A place or stead.

lieu.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *stel-der.?
Proto-Italic *s(t)lokos
Old Latin stlocus
Latin locus
Old French leu
Middle French lieubor.
English lieu
Borrowed from Middle French lieu, from Old French leu, from Latin locum, accusative of locus (“place”). Doublet of locus. Attested earlier and in Middle English only as part of the partially calqued phrase in lieu of.

ex.en: They gave him a day off in lieu of overtime pay.
ex.ja: 彼らは残業代の代わりに彼に休みを１日与えた。

note.ja: フランス語 lieu（場所）から。ラテン語 locus。in lieu of（〜の代わりに）。lieutenant と同じ。

en: The state or property of being liquid.
The degree of which something is in high supply and demand, making it easily convertible to cash.

liquidity.ety: From liquid + -ity, from Latin liquiditas. In their financial and economic senses, this and various associated terms all involve portraying assets figuratively as if they were liquids and solids, dissolving the solids with solvents, freezing and thawing, and so on.

ex.en: The bank faced a liquidity crisis.
ex.ja: その銀行は資金繰りの危機に直面した。

note.ja: liquid（液体の・現金化しやすい）+ -ity。「流動性」。

en: A low- to medium-viscosity topical preparation intended for application to unbroken skin.
To cover or treat with a lotion.

lotion.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin lōtiōnembor.
Middle English locion
English lotion
Inherited from Middle English locion, borrowed from Latin lōtiōnem. See lave. Doublet of lavation.

ex.en: She is putting on some face lotion.
ex.ja: 彼女は化粧水をつけている。

ex.en: I need hand lotion.
ex.ja: ハンドローションが欲しいのよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 lotio（洗うこと）から。lavare（洗う）。「ローション」。lavatory、laundry と同系。

en: Of or pertaining to the theology of Martin Luther (1483–1546) or his followers, or the Lutheran church.
A member of any of the Christian churches which identify with the theology of Martin Luther.

Lutheran.ety:
From the surname of German theologian and ecclesiastical reformer Martin Luther (1483–1546) + -an. Probably immediately from Renaissance Latin Lutheranus, or German Lutheraner.
Luther is from an Old High German given name, from liut (“people”) + heri (“army”) (from Proto-Germanic *harjaz (“army; commander, warrior”), from Proto-Indo-European *kóryos (“war; troops”), from *ker- (“army”)).

ex.en: She grew up in a Lutheran family.
ex.ja: 彼女はルター派の家庭で育った。

note.ja: 宗教改革者マルティン・ルター（Martin Luther）の名前から。

en: The criminal offence of maiming (“seriously wounding”) a person such that their ability to defend or protect themselves is weakened or co…
The criminal offence of maiming a person by depriving them of the use of any of their limbs.

mayhem.ety:
The noun is derived from Late Middle English mayehem, maihem, a late form of maym, maim (“disfigurement, injury, mutilation; disfigured person”) (whence modern English maim (noun)), from Anglo-Norman mahaim, mahainne (“mutilation”), and Old French mehaing, meshaing (“bodily harm, loss of limb”).
The verb is partly:
* from Late Middle English mahaym, maheyme, a late form of maimen, maymen (“to injure seriously, mutilate, maim; to damage; to destroy; to afflict with disease; to dispossess”) (whence modern English maim (verb)), from Anglo-Norman mahaigner, mahimer, Middle French mehaignier, and O

ex.en: The fire alarm caused mayhem in the building.
ex.ja: 火災報知器が鳴って、建物の中は大混乱になった。

note.ja: 古フランス語 mahaignier（傷つける）から。maim（不具にする）と同じ。「傷害罪」→「大混乱」。

en: Wrongly; erroneously.
By accident; by mistake; in error (without intention to do so).

mistakenly.ety:
Etymology tree
English mistaken
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English mistakenly
From mistaken + -ly.

ex.en: Sorry! I mistakenly clicked on "Send".
ex.ja: ごめん！間違って「送信」クリックしちゃった。

ex.en: Sorry! I mistakenly clicked on "Send" before I was finished.
ex.ja: すみません、途中でうっかり送信ボタンを押してしまいました。

ex.en: I've mistakenly deleted the party information and registration you sent to me.
ex.ja: パーティーの案内と申込書を間違って削除してしまいました。

note.ja: mistaken（誤った）+ -ly。「誤って」。

en: Commonwealth standard spelling of mold.
Commonwealth standard spelling of mold.

mould.ety: Via Middle English molde, moulde (“mould, cast”) and Old French modle, from Latin modulus.

ex.en: There was mould on the old bread.
ex.ja: 古いパンにカビが生えていた。

note.ja: mold のイギリスのつづり。

ex.ja: 神経科学は私たちがどのように学ぶかを理解するのに役立つ。

en: Of, having, or relating to nostalgia.
A person who displays nostalgia for something.

ex.en: This game is so nostalgic.
ex.ja: このゲーム、めっちゃ懐かしい。

ex.en: There's something nostalgic about walking the shopping district in the evening.
ex.ja: 夕暮れの商店街を歩くと、どこか懐かしい気持ちになる。

ex.en: The orchestra struck up nostalgic music.
ex.ja: 管弦楽団は郷愁に満ちた音楽を演奏し始めた。

note.ja: nostalgia（郷愁）+ -ic。ギリシャ語 nostos（帰郷）+ algos（痛み）。「懐かしい」。

en: Burdensome or difficult to bear.
Tyrannical or exercising unjust power.

oppressive.ety:
Etymology tree

From oppress + -ive.

ex.en: He defies the present government which is no less oppressive than its predecessor.
ex.ja: 彼は、前の政府に劣らず圧制的な現政府に公然と反抗している。

note.ja: oppress + -ive。「圧制的な・重苦しい」。

en: The act of providing approval and support; backing; championship.
Customers collectively; clientele; business.
To support by being a patron of.
To be a regular customer or client of; to patronize

patronage.ety: From Middle English patronage, from Old French patronage (modern French patronage). Equivalent to patron + -age. Piecewise doublet of patternage.

ex.en: We really thank you for your patronage.
ex.ja: 日頃のご愛顧にお礼申し上げます。

ex.en: Thank you for your patronage.
ex.ja: 毎度ごひいきにありがとうございます。

note.ja: patron（後援者）+ -age。ラテン語 patronus（保護者）、pater（父）。「後援・ひいき」。

en: The highest point.
A tall, sharp and craggy rock or mountain.
To place on a pinnacle.
To build or furnish with a pinnacle or pinnacles.

pinnacle.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French pinacle, pinnacle, from Late Latin pinnāculum (“a peak, pinnacle”), from Latin pinna (“a pinnacle”); see pin. Doublet of panache.

ex.en: Winning the gold medal was the pinnacle of her career.
ex.ja: 金メダル獲得は彼女の競技人生の頂点だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 pinnaculum（小さな羽・尖塔）から。pinna（羽）。「尖塔」→「頂点」。

en: To be successful; to succeed; to be fortunate or prosperous; to thrive; to make gain.
To grow; to increase.

prosper.ety: From Old French prosperer, from Latin prosperō (“to render happy”), from prosperus (“prosperous”), from Proto-Italic *prosparos, from Proto-Indo-European *speh₁- (“to succeed”), whence also Latin spēs (“hope, expectation”).

ex.en: The good will not necessarily prosper.
ex.ja: 善人が必ずしも成功するとは限らない。

ex.en: Not all good men will prosper.
ex.ja: 善人必ずしも栄える者でない。

ex.en: My business is prospering.
ex.ja: 私の商売は繁盛している。

note.ja: ラテン語 prosperare（成功させる）から。pro + spes（希望）。「希望どおりになる」→「栄える」。prosperity。

en: A trembling or shaking.
An earthquake, a trembling of the ground with force.
To tremble or shake.
To be in a state of fear, shock, amazement, etc., such as might cause one to tremble.

quake.ety: From Middle English quaken, from Old English cwacian (“to quake, tremble, chatter”), from Proto-Germanic *kwakōną (“to shake, quiver, tremble”), itself likely of imitative origin. Related to Old English cweċċan (“to shake, swing, move, vibrate, shake off, give up”) (see quitch), Dutch kwakkelen (“to ail, be ailing”), German Quackelei (“chattering”), Danish kvakle (“to bungle”), Latin vexō (“toss, shake violently, jostle, vex”), Irish bogadh (“a move, movement, shift, change”).

ex.en: The quake shook the whole city.
ex.ja: 地震が街全体を揺らした。

note.ja: 古英語 cwacian（震える）から。「震える」→ earthquake（地震）の短縮。

en: Of descriptions or distinctions based on some quality rather than on some quantity.
Of a form of analysis that yields the identity of a compound.
Something qualitative.

qualitative.ety: From Late Latin (or Medieval Latin) quālitātīvus. Equivalent to quality + -ative.

ex.en: The study used qualitative interviews.
ex.ja: その研究では質的なインタビューを用いた。

note.ja: ラテン語 qualitas（性質）から。qualis（どのような）。「質的な」。quantitative（量的な）と対。

A racehorse.

en: Arranged like rays that radiate from, or converge to, a common centre.
Of, or relating to a radius (line joining to a geometric centre).
An item in a radial configuration, such as a spoke of a wheel.
One of a set of earthing wires arranged radially around the base of a wireless antenna.

radial.ety: From Medieval Latin radiālis (“radial”), from Latin radius. By surface analysis, radius + -al.

ex.en: The city has a radial pattern of streets.
ex.ja: その都市の道路は放射状に広がっている。

note.ja: radius（半径）+ -al。ラテン語 radius（光線・車輪の輻）。radio と同じ。

en: To seal (something) again with a cap.
To replace the worn tread on a tire by gluing on a new outer portion.
A tire that has had new tread glued on.

ex.en: Let's recap what we learned today.
ex.ja: 今日学んだことをおさらいしよう。

note.ja: recapitulate（要点を繰り返す）の短縮。ラテン語 capitulum（小さな見出し）。「要約」。chapter と同じ語源。

ex.ja: その歌手の声はすぐにそれと分かる。

en: The act of scouting or exploring (especially military or medical) to gain information.

reconnaissance.ety: Borrowed from French reconnaissance (“recognition”). Doublet of recognizance.

ex.en: The plane flew a reconnaissance mission.
ex.ja: その飛行機は偵察任務についた。

note.ja: フランス語 reconnaissance（見分けること）から。re + connaître（知る）。「偵察」。recognize と同じ。

en: One who rules in place of the monarch, especially because the monarch is too young, absent, or disabled.
A member of a municipal or civic body of governors, especially in certain European cities.
Ruling; governing; regnant.
Exercising vicarious authority.

regent.ety: From Middle English regent, from Anglo-Norman regent, Middle French regent, and their source, Latin regēns (“ruling; ruler, governor, prince”), present participle of regō (“to govern, to steer”).

ex.en: The queen's uncle ruled as regent.
ex.ja: 女王のおじが摂政として統治した。

note.ja: reg（支配する）+ ent（人）。（王に代わって）支配する人 →「摂政・（大学の）理事」。

en: In a reluctant or hesitant manner.

reluctantly.ety:
Etymology tree
English reluctant
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English reluctantly
From reluctant + -ly.

ex.en: He went to see her reluctantly.
ex.ja: 彼はいやいや彼女に会いに行った。

ex.en: He reluctantly agreed to my proposal.
ex.ja: 彼は僕の提案にしぶしぶ同意した。

ex.en: She reluctantly agreed to our proposal.
ex.ja: 彼女は我々の提案にしぶしぶ同意した。

note.ja: reluctant（気が進まない）+ -ly。re + luctari（もがく）。「しぶしぶ」。

en: An interpretation or performance of an artwork, especially a musical score or musical work.
A given visual reproduction of something.
To surrender or hand over (a person or thing); especially, for one jurisdiction to do so to another.

rendition.ety: From obsolete French rendition, alteration (after rendre (“to render”)) of reddition (“reddition”). Many senses influenced by render.

ex.en: She sang a beautiful rendition of the old song.
ex.ja: 彼女はその古い歌を美しく歌い上げた。

note.ja: render（表現する・引き渡す）+ -ition。ラテン語 reddere（返す）。「演奏・表現・引き渡し」。

The area on either side of a road.

ex.ja: 彼はのたれ死にをしてしまった。

ex.ja: 我々はその夜、ロードサイドパークで寝た。

note.ja: road（道）+ side（わき）。「道端」。

en: Mixed, disordered, shuffled.
Beaten and cooked.

ex.ja: 選手達はボールを奪い合った。

ex.ja: 彼らは路上で１ペニー硬貨を奪い合った。

ex.en: Tom made some scrambled eggs.
ex.ja: トムはスクランブルエッグを作った。

note.ja: scramble（かき混ぜる・よじ登る）+ -ed。scrambled eggs（いり卵）。

en: The office or department of a government secretary.
A kind of dicastery within the Roman Curia.

ex.en: The secretariat of the conference is in Geneva.
ex.ja: その会議の事務局はジュネーブにある。

note.ja: secretary（秘書）+ -iat。「秘書官の職」→「事務局」。

en: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together.
To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through pieces of fabric in order to join them together.

sew.ety: From Middle English sewen, sowen, from Old English siwian, seowian, seowan (“to sew, mend, patch, knit together, link, unite”), from Proto-Germanic *siwjaną (“to sew”), from Proto-Indo-European *syewH- (“to sew”). Cognate with Scots sew, North Frisian saie, sei, Saterland Frisian säie, Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish sy, and, more distantly, Polish szyć, Russian шить (šitʹ), Latin suō, Sanskrit सीव्यति (sī́vyati). Related to seam.

ex.en: Would you sew a button on my shirt?
ex.ja: ワイシャツにボタンをつけて。

ex.en: Tom sewed the button back on his shirt.
ex.ja: トムはシャツのボタンを付け直した。

ex.en: She sewed a button on her coat.
ex.ja: 彼女は上着にボタンを縫い付けた。

note.ja: 古英語 sīwian（縫う）から。ラテン語 suere と同じ祖先。suture（縫合）と同じ。

Nervous, anxious.

ex.ja: テーブルの脚がぐらぐらする。

ex.en: The EU's unity is gradually becoming shakier.
ex.ja: EUの統合性は徐々に怪しくなってきた。

note.ja: shake + -y。「震える・不安定な」。

en: Intended to deceive; false.
Counterfeit; unreal.
A fake; an imitation that purports to be genuine.
Trickery, hoaxing.
To deceive, cheat, lie.
To obtrude by fraud or imposition.

sham.ety:
Probably a dialectal form of shame.
Alternatively, sham is a term that is used to describe the bottom thick base of a glass, usually a wine or stem glass, where the stem meets the bulbous shape bowl. Glass manufacturers would increase the "sham" to deceive customers into thinking a glass holds more than it actually does. For example, a manufacturer would mold a 12oz glass with a larger "sham" in the base to reduce the volume of the glasses to fit 10-11oz of liquid. By increasing the bulge in the base, usually where the stem meets the glass, it is almost impossible to visually distinguish the d

ex.en: This is not a sham.
ex.ja: これはインチキじゃないよ。

note.ja: shame（恥）の方言形とされる。「見せかけ・いんちき」。

en: A deficiency or falling short; failure to attain a goal or ideal.

ex.en: You are too critical of others' shortcomings.
ex.ja: 君は他人のあらさがしをしすぎるよ。

ex.en: You're too critical of others' shortcomings.
ex.ja: 君は他人のあらさがしをしすぎるよ。

ex.en: We should be conscious of our shortcomings.
ex.ja: 自分たちの欠点を自覚するべきです。

note.ja: short（足りない）+ coming（来ること）。「期待に届かないこと」→「欠点」。

en: A killer; a murderer; someone who slays.
A butcher.

slayer.ety: From Middle English slear, sleere, sleare, slaare, dissimilated from Old English slaga (“slayer”), equivalent to slay + -er.

ex.en: In the legend, the dragon slayer saved the village.
ex.ja: 伝説では、竜を退治した者が村を救った。

note.ja: slay（殺す）+ -er。slay は古英語 slēan（打つ）。slaughter と同系。

en: Tending to soothe or mollify.
Giving relief.
The act by which somebody is soothed.

ex.en: I often listen to soothing music in order to relax.
ex.ja: リラックスできる癒し系の音楽をよく聞いている。

ex.en: In order to relax, I need to listen to soothing music.
ex.ja: リラックスするには落ち着く音楽を聞く必要がある。

note.ja: soothe（なだめる）+ -ing。「心を落ち着かせる」。

en: To produce or deposit (eggs) in water.
To generate, bring into being, especially nonmammalian beings in very large numbers.
The numerous eggs of an aquatic organism.
Mushroom mycelium prepared for (aided) propagation.

spawn.ety: Recorded since 1413; from Middle English spawnen, from Anglo-Norman espaundre, from Old French espandre, from Latin expandere (“stretch out; spread out”, verb). Doublet of expand. Compare also Middle English spalden, spolden, spawden (“to cut open (a fish)”).

ex.en: What might a planet need to spawn life?
ex.ja: 惑星が命を生み出すために何が必要だろうか。

ex.en: Most salmon die after spawning.
ex.ja: サケは産卵後、ほとんどが死んでしまいます。

note.ja: 古フランス語 espandre（撒き散らす）から。ラテン語 expandere。「卵をまく」→「生み出す」。expand と同じ。

en: A person who engages in stalking, i.e., quietly approaching animals to be hunted; a tracker or guide in hunting game.
A person who secretly follows someone, sometimes with unlawful intentions.

stalker.ety: From Middle English stalkere, equivalent to stalk + -er.

ex.en: You're practically a stalker.
ex.ja: ストーカーみたい。

note.ja: stalk（忍び寄る）+ -er。「ストーカー」。

en: A person or animal's natural height when standing upright.
Respect (social standing) coming from achievement or development.

stature.ety: From Middle English stature, from Old French stature, from Latin statūra.

ex.en: Young people have shown a lot of improvement in physical stature.
ex.ja: 若者は非常に身長の伸びを見せた。

ex.en: The boy did not reach his father's stature of six feet.
ex.ja: その子は６フィートという父親の身長に達しなかった。

ex.en: She's small in stature, but immense in intellect.
ex.ja: 彼女は背が低いが、知的だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 statura（立った高さ）から。sta（立つ）。→「身長・名声（立派さ）」。

en: A person who manages the property or affairs for another entity.
A chief administrator of a medieval manor.
To act as the steward or caretaker of (something)

steward.ety: From Middle English steward, stiward, from Old English stiġweard (“steward, housekeeper, one who has the superintendence of household affairs, guardian”), from stiġ (“a wooden enclosure; house, hall”) + weard (“ward, guard, guardian, keeper”), equivalent to sty + ward. Compare Icelandic stívarður (“steward”). More at sty, ward.

ex.en: "Here you are," the steward says.
ex.ja: 「どうぞ」と乗務員が言います。

note.ja: 古英語 stigweard ＝ stig（家・豚小屋）+ weard（番人）。「家の番人」→「管理人・客室乗務員」。

en: Large; bulky.
Firm; resolute; dauntless.
A dark and strong malt brew made with toasted grain.
A serving of this beer.

stout.ety:
From Middle English stoute, from Old French estout (“brave, fierce, proud”) (Modern French dialectal stout (“proud”)), from earlier Old French estolt (“strong”), from Frankish *stolt, *stult (“bold, proud”), from Proto-Germanic *stultaz (“bold, proud”), from Proto-Indo-European *stel- (“to put, stand”).
Cognate with Dutch stout (“stout, bold, naughty”), Low German stolt (“stately, proud”), German stolz (“proud, haughty, arrogant, stately”), Old Norse stoltr (“proud”) (Danish stolt (“proud”), Icelandic stoltur (“proud”)).
Meaning "strong in body, powerfully built" was first attested in c. 1386,

ex.en: The defenders put up a stout resistance.
ex.ja: 防衛者達は強い抵抗を見せた。

ex.en: He got so stout that his collar did not meet.
ex.ja: あまり太ったのでカラーの前が合わなかった。

ex.en: He looked small beside my father's stout body.
ex.ja: がっしりした私の父の隣にいて、彼は小さく見えた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 estout（勇敢な）から。「頑丈な・太った」→ 濃いビール →「スタウト」。

A chemical or tool used to remove paint, sheathing, etc. from something.

en: The remains of something that has been cut off; especially the remains of a tree, the remains of a limb.
The place or occasion at which a campaign takes place; the husting.
To stop, confuse, or puzzle.
To baffle; to make unable to find an answer to a question or problem.

stump.ety:
From Middle English stumpe, stompe (“stump”), from or akin to Middle Low German stump (“stump”) or Middle Dutch stomp, from Old Saxon or Old Dutch *stump, from Proto-West Germanic *stump, from Proto-Germanic *stumpaz (“stump, blunt, part cut off”). Displaced native Old English stofn.
Cognate with Middle Dutch stomp (“stump”), Old High German stumph (“stump”) (German Stumpf), Old Norse stumpr (“stump”). More at stop.

ex.en: He was stumped by the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題で閉口していた。

ex.en: But I have nothing left. I am just an old stump.
ex.ja: でも、私には何も残ってない、ただの古い切り株です。

ex.en: The French teacher was stumped by her student's question.
ex.ja: フランス語の先生は生徒の質問に立ち往生した。

note.ja: 中低ドイツ語 stump（切り株）から。「切り株」→ 選挙運動で切り株の上で演説した（stump speech）。

en: Placed in a lower class, rank, or position.
Submissive or inferior to, or controlled by authority.
One who is subordinate.
A hyponym.
To embed (a clause) into another clause that is the main one.
To make of lower priority in order of payment in bankruptcy.

subordinate.ety: From Middle English subordinat, from Medieval Latin subōrdinātus, past participle of subōrdināre, from sub- + ōrdināre (“to order”).

ex.en: He is able to subordinate passion to reason.
ex.ja: 彼は理性で情欲を制することが出来る。

ex.en: All the other issues are subordinate to this one.
ex.ja: 他の問題はこの問題ほど重要ではない。

ex.en: He growled out orders to his subordinates.
ex.ja: 彼は部下にどなって命令をした。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ ordin（順序）+ ate。順序が下の →「下位の・部下・従属させる」。

en: A place of worship for Jews.
A congregation of Jews for the purpose of worship or religious study.

synagogue.ety: Inherited from Middle English synagoge, from Old French synagoge, from Latin synagōga, from Ancient Greek σῠνᾰγωγή (sŭnăgōgḗ, “assembly, gathering”), from συνάγω (sunágō, “to gather together”), from σῠ́ν (sŭ́n, “with, together”) & ᾰ̓́γω (ắgō, “to lead”). By surface analysis, syn- + -agogue.

ex.en: They went to the synagogue on Saturday.
ex.ja: 彼らは土曜日にシナゴーグへ行った。

note.ja: syn（共に）+ agogue（導く・集める）。共に集まる場所 →「シナゴーグ（ユダヤ教の会堂）」。ag（行う・駆る）と同じ祖先。

en: A trial; an experiment; an attempt.
A schedule for an event or a programme.
Of or pertaining to a trial or trials; essaying; experimental.
Uncertain; subject to future change.

tentative.ety: From Medieval Latin tentātīvus (“trying, testing”), from tentō, past participle tentātus (“to try, test”); see tent, tempt.

ex.en: Attached is the tentative agenda.
ex.ja: 仮の議事内容を送付しました。

note.ja: ラテン語 tentare（試す）から。試しの →「仮の・ためらいがちな」。attempt（試みる）も同じ。

Relating to a topic or subject of current interest.
A substance, especially a medication, applied externally (to the surface of the skin or eye).
A topical anaesthetic.

en: Restless; disturbed by pain, anxiety.
Not easy in manner; constrained

uneasy.ety: From Middle English unesy, equivalent to un- + easy. Merged with Middle English unethe, uneathe (“difficult, not easy”). See uneath.

ex.en: I felt cold and uneasy all night.
ex.ja: 一晩中寒くて不安でした。

ex.en: I didn't feel uneasy when I read the letter.
ex.ja: その手紙を読んだとき、私は不安を感じなかった。

ex.en: I am uneasy about the future of this country.
ex.ja: この国の将来が心配です。

note.ja: un（否定）+ easy（気楽な）。「不安な」。

en: To undo a folding.
To become unfolded.
In functional programming, a kind of higher-order function that is the opposite of a fold.

unfold.ety: From Middle English unfolden, from Old English unfealdan (“to unfold”), equivalent to un- + fold.

ex.en: At last he unfolded his plans for their future.
ex.ja: とうとう彼は彼らの将来に対する計画を打ち明けた。

ex.en: I unfolded the map on the desk.
ex.ja: 私は机の上に地図を広げた。

ex.en: The story unfolded just how I expected.
ex.ja: 俺が予想した通りの展開になってきたな。

note.ja: un（元に戻す）+ fold（たたむ）。「広げる」→「展開する・明らかになる」。

en: The act of varying or the state of being variable.
A difference between what is expected and what is observed; deviation.

variance.ety: From Middle English variance, variaunce, equivalent to vary + -ance, from Old French variance or directly from Anglo-Latin variaunce, veriaunce, wariaunce; all from Latin variantia.

ex.en: There is a large variance in prices between stores.
ex.ja: 店によって価格に大きなばらつきがある。

note.ja: vary（変わる）+ -ance。ラテン語 variare。「相違・ばらつき・分散」。various と同じ。

en: The length of a single cycle of a wave, as measured by the distance between one peak or trough of a wave and the next; it is often design…
A person's attitude and way of thinking as compared to another person's.

ex.en: Violet light has a shorter wavelength than red light.
ex.ja: 紫の光は、赤の光よりも短い波長です。

note.ja: wave（波）+ length（長さ）。「波長」→ on the same wavelength（気が合う）。

en: The amount of work assigned to a particular worker, normally in a specified time period.
The amount of work that a machine can handle or produce.

ex.en: My workload has doubled this month.
ex.ja: 今月は仕事量が２倍になった。

note.ja: work + load（荷）。「仕事量」。

en: Having been acquitted; having gone through a trial that resulted in something other than a guilty verdict.

ex.en: The jury acquitted him of the crime.
ex.ja: 陪審員は彼を無罪とした。

ex.en: The accused was acquitted on two of the charges.
ex.ja: 被告人は容疑のうち２つについては無罪となった。

ex.en: The court acquitted him of the charge of murder.
ex.ja: 法廷は彼のその殺人容疑について無罪とした。

note.ja: acquit（無罪にする）+ -ed。古フランス語 aquiter（借りを返す）、ラテン語 quietus（自由な）。quit と同じ。

en: Each in a string of small balls making up the rosary or paternoster.
A small, round object with a hole to allow it to be threaded on a cord or wire, particularly for decorative purposes.
To form into a bead.
To apply beads to.

bead.ety:
From Middle English bede (“a prayer”), also “a bead for counting prayers” in a peire of bedes (literally “a pair of beads”), from Old English bedu, bed, ġebed (“a request, entreaty, prayer”), from Proto-West Germanic *bedu, *bed, *gabed, from Proto-Germanic *bedō, *bedą.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Gebäd (“prayer”), Cimbrian gapéet (“prayer”), Dutch gebed and bede (“prayer”), German Gebet (“prayer”), Low German Gebett (“prayer”), Luxembourgish Gebiet (“prayer”), Vilamovian gybāt (“prayer”).

ex.en: He drew a bead on a stag at bay.
ex.ja: 彼は追いつめられたシカを銃でねらった。

note.ja: 古英語 gebed（祈り）から。数珠の玉 →「ビーズ」。

en: A place for a vessel to lie at anchor or to moor.
A room in a vessel in which the officers or company mess (“eat together”) and reside; also, a room or other place in a vessel for storage.
To bring (a ship or other vessel) into a berth (noun etymology 1, noun sense 1.1); also, to provide a berth for (a vessel).
To use a device to bring (a spacecraft) into its berth or dock.

berth.ety:
The noun is derived from Late Middle English birth (“(nautical) bearing away or off, clearance, berth”). Further etymology uncertain, but probably from beren (“to carry (away), bear”) + -th (suffix denoting a condition, quality, state of being, etc., forming nouns); if so, the English word is analysable as bear + -th (suffix forming nouns from verbs), and is a piecewise doublet of birth.
The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: I'd like to reserve a sleeping berth.
ex.ja: 寝台車を予約したいのですが。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。bear（運ぶ）と関係するとされる。「（船の）寝台・停泊所」。

en: The extortion of money or favors by threats of public accusation, critique, or exposure.
Compromising material that can be used to extort someone.
To extort money or favors from (a person) by exciting fears of injury other than bodily harm, such as injury to reputation, distress of m…
To speak ill of someone; to defame someone.

blackmail.ety:
From black + mail (“a piece of money”). Compare Middle English blak rente (“a type of blackmail levied by Irish chieftains”).
The word is variously derived from the tribute paid by English and Scottish border dwellers to border reivers in return for immunity from raids and other harassment. This tribute was paid in goods or labour, in Latin reditus nigri (“black mail”); the opposite is blanche firmes or reditus albi (“white rent”), denoting payment by silver.
McKay derives it from two Scottish Gaelic words blàthaich, pronounced (the th silent) bl-aich, "to protect" and màl (“tribute, payment”)

ex.en: Tom was blackmailed by Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーに脅迫されていた。

note.ja: black（黒い・不正な）+ mail（年貢・地代）。スコットランドの山賊が取り立てた保護料から「恐喝」。

en: The condition of being blind; unable to see.
Want of intellectual or moral discernment; mental darkness; ignorance, heedlessness.

blindness.ety: From Middle English blyndnes, blyndnesse, from Old English blindnes (“blindness”), equivalent to blind + -ness.

ex.en: He made up his mind to jog in spite of his blindness.
ex.ja: 彼は目が見えなかったがジョギングをしようと決心した。

note.ja: blind（目の見えない）+ -ness。「失明」。

en: In a bright manner.

brightly.ety: From Middle English brightliche, from Old English beorhtlice, equivalent to bright + -ly.

ex.en: We were looking at the fire burning brightly.
ex.ja: 私達は赤々と燃えている火を見つめていた。

ex.en: The moon fell brightly on the water.
ex.ja: 月光は水面を明るく照らした。

ex.en: The fire was burning brightly.
ex.ja: 火は赤々と燃えていた。

note.ja: bright（明るい）+ -ly。「明るく」。

en: The crime of unlawfully breaking into a vehicle, house, store, or other enclosure with the intent to steal.
Under the common law, breaking and entering of the dwelling of another at night with the intent to commit a felony.

burglary.ety: From New Latin burglaria. By surface analysis, burglar + -y. Displaced native Old English hūsbryċe (literally “house-breach”).

ex.en: He was arrested on the charge of burglary.
ex.ja: 彼は強盗のかどで逮捕された。

ex.en: Recently, there are a lot of burglaries around here.
ex.ja: この辺りは近頃強盗がよくはいる。

ex.en: On arriving home, I discovered the burglary.
ex.ja: 帰宅してすぐに私は泥棒に入られたことがわかった。

note.ja: burglar（泥棒）+ -y。中世ラテン語 burglator。「住居侵入（窃盗）」。

en: A restaurant in which customers select their food at a counter then carry it on a tray to a table to eat.
A dining area in an institution where meals may be purchased (as above), provided, or brought in from elsewhere.

cafeteria.ety: Borrowed from Mexican Spanish cafetería (“coffeehouse”), from cafetera (“coffee maker”), from French cafetière, from café, from Ottoman Turkish قهوه (kahve) (Turkish kahve), from Arabic قَهْوَة (qahwa, “coffee”). Doublet of cafetière.

ex.en: A cafeteria is a self-service style restaurant.
ex.ja: カフェテリアは料理を自分で取るセルフサービスのレストランです。

ex.en: I heard my name called in the cafeteria.
ex.ja: 私は食堂で自分の名前が呼ばれるのが聞こえた。

ex.en: She might be having coffee in the cafeteria.
ex.ja: 彼女はカフェテリアでコーヒーを飲んでいるかもしれない。

note.ja: メキシコのスペイン語 cafetería（コーヒー店）から。café（コーヒー）。「セルフサービスの食堂」。

en: A small, usually yellow, finch (genus Serinus), a songbird native to the Canary Islands.
Any of various small birds of different countries, most of which are largely yellow in colour.
Of a light yellow colour.
To dance nimbly (as in the canary dance).
To test a software change by rolling out to a small set of machines or users before making it available to all.

canary.ety: From French canarie, from Spanish canario, from the Latin Canariae insulae (“Canary Islands”) (Spanish Islas Canarias); from the largest island Insula Canaria (“Dog Island" or "Canine Island”), named for its dogs, from canārius (“canine”), from canis (“dog”).

ex.en: A pair of canaries are her only friends.
ex.ja: １つがいのカナリアだけが彼女の友達であった。

ex.en: We have a dog, a cat and three canaries.
ex.ja: 犬が１匹、猫が１匹、カナリヤが３羽います。

ex.en: My canary was killed by a cat.
ex.ja: 私のカナリアは猫に殺された。

note.ja: スペイン領カナリア諸島（Canary Islands）の鳥から。島名はラテン語 Canariae insulae（犬の島）。canine（犬の）と同じ。

en: Cardiovascular; pertaining to the health of the circulatory and respiratory systems.
Exercise with the goal of raising the heart rate by walking or running on the treadmill.

ex.en: I do thirty minutes of cardio every morning.
ex.ja: 私は毎朝３０分有酸素運動をしている。

note.ja: cardiovascular exercise（心肺の運動）の短縮。ギリシャ語 kardia（心臓）。「有酸素運動」。

en: Awkward, lacking coordination.
Not elegant or well-planned, lacking tact or subtlety.
A clumsy person.

clumsy.ety: Possibly from an alteration of clumsed (“benumbed”) or from clumse (“a stupid fellow; lout”) + -y. More at clumse.

ex.en: You are really clumsy, aren't you!
ex.ja: あなたは本当に不器用ですね。

ex.en: He is clumsy with his hands.
ex.ja: 彼は手先が不器用だ。

ex.en: Tom is clumsy with words.
ex.ja: トムは滑舌が悪い。

note.ja: 中英語 clumsen（かじかむ）から。「かじかんだ手のような」→「不器用な」。

en: A subatomic particle forming part of the nucleus of an atom and having no charge; it is a combination of an up quark and two down quarks.

neutron.ety: From neutral + -on; by surface analysis, neutr(o)- + -on. Coined by Scottish-Australian physicist William Sutherland in 1899 in a paper in the Philosophical Magazine. Subsequent usage was sporadic and theoretical, sometimes referring to neutrinos rather than neutrons, and the modern sense was reintroduced alongside proton by Ernest Rutherford in 1920.

ex.en: Atoms are composed of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
ex.ja: 原子は陽子・中性子・電子で構成されている。

note.ja: neutral（中性の）+ -on。「電気的に中性の粒子」→「中性子」。
